summary: ‏Silent Frontier is an interactive, online web experience built in Figma for school-age space enthusiasts to bring NASA’s dormant Moon and Mars explorers back to life. Featuring original hand-drawn spacecraft characters created by our team, the game casts players as Archive Recovery Specialists who explore the Moon (Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles) and Mars (Sojourner Rover and Ingenuity Helicopter). Using official NASA mission data, each spacecraft shares its engineering and scientific discoveries in the first person, challenging players with quick quizzes to unlock all 3 Archive Keys.
details:
What is Silent Frontier?

Silent Frontier is an interactive, story-driven web prototype that brings historic NASA Moon and Mars hardware to life. It transforms technical archives into engaging first-person stories for young space enthusiasts.

How Does It Work?

Players become Archive Recovery Specialists:

1. Free Exploration: Choose between the Moon and Mars.

2. First-Person Narratives: Meet the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles (LRVs), Sojourner Rover, and Ingenuity Helicopter. Each shares its story, engineering design, and scientific contributions.

3. Interactive Quizzes & Keys: Answer science questions to unlock Archive Keys and restore all three historic records.

Creativity, Tools & Development

1. Original Artwork: All spacecraft characters, planetary visuals, and UI elements were hand-drawn by our team, creating a warm, engaging experience with a dark-purple cosmic aesthetic.

2. Software & Prototyping: Designed and prototyped as an interactive online web experience using Figma and Clip Studio Paint.

3. Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure: AI assisted in refining first-person narratives based on official NASA data. All visual artwork, character illustrations, and UI designs are 100% human-made by our team.

4. We used canva templates for the demo

Our goal is to make space history accessible, memorable, and inspiring by allowing young learners to discover the stories behind humanity’s pioneering machines.
